lede: Engineering case studies from paid work first. Homelab is labelled as practice, not Staff evidence.

items.name: SAWIS BI
items.problem: The client runs wine-industry business intelligence that depends on large import and export jobs hitting a live MySQL database. When a job fails, the business is stuck until the data path is understood and recovered.
items.responsibility: I am Tech Lead for the PHP application and the database work. I own the job path and recovery. I do not own servers, CI, or cloud accounts for SAWIS.
items.decisions: Keep the system as an application-and-data problem I can diagnose end to end: PHP job, MySQL state, failed batch — not a platform rewrite I do not own.
items.leadership: I own the technical work on this client. Full support for the site; not a 24/7 on-call rota.
items.outcome: Failed import/export jobs get a recovered data path rather than a patch that hides the cause. No public volume metrics.
items.blurb: Tech Lead on wine-industry BI: PHP + MySQL import/export. I recover failed jobs. I do not own infra.

items.name: Indawo
items.role: Client owner — application and guest OS
items.stack: PHP, Laravel / legacy PHP, MySQL, Docker, Azure VM, PR deploys
items.problem: A production PHP site had to keep running for a client I own. Hardware under the original on-prem CentOS host died. Later the app needed a durable home that I could still operate.
items.responsibility: I own spec, cost, plan, build, and sign-off. I manage the application and guest OS. I do not manage Azure hardware or the cloud account. I coordinate a PM, a senior developer, and a mid developer (not line manager).
items.decisions: On the dead host I containerised the legacy app with Docker on spare CentOS and fixed publishing/networking so production came back the same weekend. The app now runs on an Azure VM; I operate the guest, not the account.
items.leadership: I am the client-facing engineer: new work is scoped and costed with the client, then built and reviewed with the team until they are happy. Invoicing stays on track.
items.outcome: Site restored after hardware loss; still in production on Azure under my application ownership. Delivery path: PRs and a ~10 minute post-deploy health window.
items.blurb: I own this client: spec to sign-off. Docker restore after hardware death. Azure guest OS, not the account.

items.name: tf-fleet-iac (Siyabonwa)
items.role: Freelance with a friend — AWS as code
items.stack: Terraform, EC2, RDS MySQL 8.4, CodePipeline, CCS
items.problem: A production truck-management PHP app needed a reproducible AWS environment, not a snowflake box.
items.responsibility: I defined the AWS stack in Terraform (af-south-1) with a friend. This is freelance, not Overdrive's Indawo path.
items.decisions: VPC, EC2, RDS MySQL, CodePipeline in code so the environment can be rebuilt.
items.leadership: Shared freelance delivery, not an internal Staff mandate.
items.outcome: Live at fleet.wiums.co.za. Public IaC at github.com/EttieneW/tf-fleet-iac.
items.blurb: Freelance Terraform for a production PHP fleet. Public repo. Not how Overdrive runs Indawo.

items.name: Homelab streaming
items.problem: I do not get industry Kubernetes or a metrics platform at work.
items.responsibility: I run a private streaming stack and treat uptime as my problem.
items.decisions: Docker on Linux today; k3s/k3d to learn cluster failure. Not a public product.
items.outcome: Two years of breaking and fixing my own k3s. Labeled homelab — not Staff evidence.
items.blurb: Private streaming stack. Homelab k3s. Practice toward reliability, not a product.
